justification: Deletes an invented default lot frontage from a LIVE surface: app/assessment/page.tsx:563 mounts StateLevelControls, which mounts HousingSEPPEligibilityCard. Unlike PR #1230, a user could see this. Not Critical: the figure fed an eligibility display, not a write, a migration or a served regulatory quote, and the fix is predominantly deletion of a constant that was defeating a guard the component already had. Not Minor: it changes which housing types a property is shown as eligible for, narrows a component prop from number to number|null, and changes when the whole LMR section renders.

pre_impl.existing_data: HousingSEPPEligibilityCard already handled a missing frontage correctly: its useEffect skips the eligibility fetch on a falsy lotWidth and the component renders a card asking for lot size and frontage width. It also already carries an assessmentStatus of not_assessed, added earlier for exactly this shape of problem. The default of 15 metres meant those guards never ran, so the fix is mostly deletion rather than new logic.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I reported to the user that the page printed Frontage 15.0m in the amber panel. Reading the code showed that was wrong: the amber panel renders only when lmrFrontageStatus returns a non-empty excluded list, and a 15 clears all three minimums, so that panel returned null and printed nothing at all. The real harm there is suppression of the caveat, not a wrong number. The wrong number was printed by the eligibility card instead, at a different line. Both are now covered, and the mutation harness separately disproved a third assumption of mine by showing one display line is unreachable.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One constant deleted, one fallback removed, one prop widened to nullable, one explanatory note added. The LMR section gate was changed from isLMRArea && lotSize && lotWidth to isLMRArea && lotSize: keeping lotWidth in that condition would have newly hidden the entire section for every property whose frontage is unknown, because the invented 15 had made the condition always true. That would trade a false answer for a silent one, so the section stays and the card inside asks for the frontage.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The suite goes red if the constant returns to the shipped NSW_PLANNING_CONSTANTS object under its own name or a renamed one, if any width is substituted at the end of the lotWidth chain, if the LMR section is gated on lotWidth again, if the not-checked note is removed, or if the eligibility fetch runs without a frontage.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 20 of 20 tests pass on clean code; npx tsc --noEmit exits 0; the full frontend suite is 119 suites and 1709 tests with 0 failures. The evidence is the mutation harness: 8 mutations applied one at a time and reverted byte-for-byte, 8 of 8 CAUGHT, 0 holes. It found two real holes on the way, neither of which review had spotted: asserting the bare name positiveFiniteOrNull passed even after the call was replaced by an inline passthrough, because the function's own DEFINITION matched; and leaving a 15 fallback INSIDE the normaliser call reinstated the original defect exactly, since 15 is positive and finite, while every other assertion still passed. Both are closed -- the call site is now required by its assignment, and the chain is sliced and asserted to hold no numeric fallback. A ninth candidate is UNCATCHABLE and is recorded as such in both the harness and the suite rather than being quietly dropped.

functions.name: lmrFrontageStatus
functions.input: A frontage in metres, now only ever a figure taken from cadastral geometry rather than a substituted default, because the caller guards on null before calling it.
functions.output: Two lists, excluded and eligible, built by comparing that frontage against the three LMR minimums of 12, 12 and 15 metres.
functions.if_none: Unchanged and still takes a plain number; the null case is handled by the caller, which renders an explicit not-checked note instead of calling this at all.

functions.name: StateLevelControls lotWidth resolution
functions.input: The battleaxe-aware cadastral width, then the geometry frontage, then the estimated width, then the constraints width, each tried in order.
functions.output: A measured frontage in metres when any source holds one, typed explicitly as number or null so the compiler keeps the nullability.
functions.if_none: Null. It used to be 15, which cleared every LMR minimum; now the component states that the frontage minimums have not been checked.

functions.name: HousingSEPPEligibilityCard
functions.input: zoneCode, lotSize and lotWidth, with lotWidth now typed as number or null to match what the caller can actually supply.
functions.output: The eligibility list fetched from the housing-sepp route, together with a property summary line that prints the frontage it was given.
functions.if_none: Skips the fetch entirely and renders a card saying lot size and frontage width are needed, which is the guard the deleted constant had been defeating.

verdicts.finding: MEDIUM null-guard, StateLevelControls.tsx:1029 -- the missing-frontage notice checks only for null while the adjacent eligibility logic treats every falsy width as missing, so a 0 or NaN sentinel is handled inconsistently and partially silently.
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED and FIXED. Read the code to check rather than taking it on trust: the nullish operator only falls through on null and undefined, so an upstream 0 sentinel or a parseFloat NaN survived the chain, and the result was worse than inconsistent, it was silent. The null check was false so the new not-checked notice was hidden, and the truthiness check was false so the amber panel was hidden too, leaving no frontage text anywhere beside a card separately asking for a frontage. A positiveFiniteOrNull helper now normalises the chain, so anything that is not a positive finite number becomes null. Four assertions and two mutations cover it, and chasing this finding is what exposed the two test holes described in observed_red.
